newsitem.title: USA: US Midcon prods jump with NYMEX in paltry trade.
newsitem.headline: US Midcon prods jump with NYMEX in paltry trade.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent refined products prices jumped sharply with June NYMEX futures on Monday, with differentials narrowly mixed in slim trade as many players flocked to an industry event in southern California.

Group Three conventional unleaded gasoline diffs were little changed from late last week, with offers of 4.25 cents over June futures, although Chicago material saw diffs ease a half cent as June NYMEX settled 1.58 cent higher.
A Midwest trader said gasoline diffs in the Group Three market better withstood the sharp NYMEX upswing "because the group market is operating on fumes, inventories are so low."

And continued delays in receiving Explorer Pipeline barrels from the Gulf Coast are offering especially good price support in the Group, the trader said, adding the delayed shipments meant less material was being stored in the Williams System that feeds the Midwest.
"There's only an 18- or 19-day supply in the Williams, whereas a comfortable level would be 22-25 days," the trader said.
Differentials held stable, meanwhile, on Group Three low sulfur diesel and edged slightly lower in the Chicago market amid a robust 2.13-cent gain in June heating oil futures.
Traders predicted activity would remain lackluster for much of the week, as players attend other industry functions in New York and in Las Vegas, Nevada.
